findings.reason: The protected solution is the conventional implicit decimal-prefix trie traversal. subtree_size, prefix, first, following, size, and remaining expose the prefix interval and one-based-rank conversion directly; skip and descend branches mirror lexicographic preorder. No inert candidate would materially improve its clarity or complexity.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 440 and its Python two-integer surface. The executable solve signature and native findKthNumber method accept the same inclusive bound and one-based rank and return the selected integer. The modular Reference preserves both current source examples, the complete displayed order in the first explanation, and the single chained constraint.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064820556. Both implementations count the same clipped decimal-prefix intervals through n + 1, start at prefix 1 with k - 1 remaining moves, compare the same subtree size, skip the same sibling or descend to the same child, and return the same prefix; only the required wrapper differs.

The 512-, 2048-, and 8192-value tiers span 16x and request the final lexicographic position, forcing a materialize-and-sort alternative to process the whole range. The Approach exactly models lexicographic order as prefix preorder, derives clipped subtree sizes from adjacent prefix boundaries, explains the k - 1 offset and skip-versus-descend updates, proves rank preservation, and matches O(d^2) time with O(1) auxiliary space.
